findings.claim: The addon validator checks the 200-character tag cap only on the tags it keeps after lower()-deduplication, while the core request model checks it on every stripped raw tag before deduplication, so the two validators can still disagree on the same input.
findings.impact: A filter whose dropped duplicate is over 200 characters but whose kept spelling is not (possible only where lower() changes string length, e.g. U+0130 'İ' lowers to two code points) is accepted by the addon. The core then answers 422, the addon turns that into 503, and the frontend silently shows no meaning hits. Reaching this needs a tag over 200 characters made of length-changing capitals, which is crafted input that normal personal use does not produce.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/app/file_matching.py:61-73 deduplicates first (line 65-68) and runs the length check on the deduplicated list (line 72). backend/app/routers/internal.py:633-641 runs the length check on each raw tag (line 637) before setdefault (line 641). The r1 verifier recorded the same ordering divergence. The fix commit changed only the fold function, not this ordering.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. Reasoning: tags = ['İ'*101, 'i̇'*101]. Both lower() to the same 202-code-point string. The addon keeps the first (101 characters) and accepts. The core sees the second raw tag at 202 characters and answers 422.

bucket_proposal.reason: This touches I10's 'accept and reject the same inputs', but it can only be reached with crafted input outside the declared threat model (a single user and no adversary).

findings.proposed_fix: Check the length on every raw stripped tag before deduplicating in file_matching.py, in the same order as the core.

findings.claim: The casefold-only parity row was added only to the addon's INVALID_FILTERS table. The core's test_internal_files_matching.py has no row with a fold-sensitive pair, so nothing pins the core validator's fold.
findings.impact: Changing the core's validate_tags (or apply_file_filters' by_fold) from lower() to casefold() would reintroduce the r1 I10 divergence from the other side, and no core test would fail. The 'Layer 2 parity table' is two hand-maintained lists, not one table run against both models.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/tests/test_filtered_search_contract.py:176-179 is the only occurrence of 'straße'/'STRASSE' in any *.py test (Grep over the repository). The TestRequestCaps cases in backend/tests/test_internal_files_matching.py use ASCII tags only (t0..t20, 'x'*n).
findings.repro: Mutation (in thought): backend/app/routers/internal.py:641 `tag.lower()` -> `tag.casefold()`. The backend caps tests still pass (ASCII only), and the addon tests do not exercise the core model. Survives.

bucket_proposal.reason: This is a test gap. The current code satisfies I10 for this input. The gap only lets a future regression through.

findings.proposed_fix: Add to backend TestRequestCaps the same row: 19 ASCII tags + ['straße','STRASSE'] -> 422.

findings.claim: docs/specs/filtered-semantic-search.md:172 still says 'then the caps of 10 apply' (and section 2 says 'over the caps in 10'), while both validators and the now-corrected docs/addons/intelligence.md use 20 tags / 200 characters / 8 kinds.
findings.impact: A reader who treats the approved spec as the reference could lower TAG_MAX_COUNT or _MATCHING_MAX_TAGS to 10. That would break I10 parity and reject valid 11-20-tag queries. The fix commit corrected only the addon guide.
findings.evidence: docs/specs/filtered-semantic-search.md:172 'alias, then the caps of 10 apply.' versus addons/intelligence/app/file_matching.py:27 TAG_MAX_COUNT = 20, backend/app/routers/internal.py:57 _MATCHING_MAX_TAGS = 20, and spec section 10 itself ('at most 20 tags').

bucket_proposal.reason: This is prose contradicting code that could lead to a wrong code change. It breaks no invariant.

findings.proposed_fix: Delete 'of 10' / 'in 10' so the sentences refer to the caps in section 10. The spec is hash-approved, so this needs re-approval.
